chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from 'Abd Allah ibn Talhah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who inflicted upon another man a wound of the type muwdihah, then reparation for it was sought, but he remitted it to him,
then it worsened in him and killed him. He said: “He is liable for the diyah, except for the value of the muwdihah, because he remitted that to him, and he did not remit the life.”

key_terms.مُوضِحَةً: a head or facial wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.وَهَبَهَا: he remitted or granted away the claim relating to it
key_terms.يُطْلَبُ: compensation or claim is sought for the injury
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةِ: blood money due for unlawful killing or injury

ai.seo_question: If someone forgives compensation for a wound and the victim later dies from it, is the assailant still liable for the diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury that later leads to death. If the injured person remits compensation for the original wound, that remission applies only to the wound itself and does not cancel liability for the later loss of life.
